bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Low-cost import competition — The BRSR material-issues table flags cheap imports from China and ASEAN as putting pressure on domestic prices and margins, with negative financial implication. The Board's Report independently describes the year as marked by continued import pressure from low-cost origins and subdued realisations across certain product segments, and turnover was marginally lower on net sales realisation pressure. Mitigation is quality differentiation, focus on specification-driven customers and pursuit of trade-remedy support through industry associations.
- Raw material availability and price volatility (pulp, wastepaper, chemicals) — This is the structural exposure of a non-integrated mill. Pulp, wastepaper, chemicals and packaging inputs are exposed to global commodity and domestic price volatility, and the MD&A risk table adds that fluctuations in global pulp and wastepaper prices may impact input costs and margins. Mitigation is a diversified sourcing strategy across geographies and suppliers, long-term arrangements, term contracts with selective spot purchases, inventory planning and selective hedging.
- Currency risk on USD-linked imports — USD-linked imports create a mismatch against INR revenues; rupee depreciation increases landed input cost. This is amplified by the quality-led model built on imported virgin wood pulp and imported machinery, against exports of only about 5% of turnover, so there is little natural offset. Mitigation is hedging through forward contracts and other approved instruments under the treasury policy, plus natural hedging mechanisms.
- Regulatory and environmental compliance burden — Compliance with effluent, EPR, ZLD and environmental norms requires continuous investment, and the Company is subject to evolving environmental laws which may impact operations. Mitigation is a dedicated compliance team, internal audit review and management systems aligned with relevant certifications, supported by continuous monitoring and process upgrades.
- Water availability and water management — Water is a critical input for paper manufacturing, and scarcity, cost escalation or regulatory restrictions can affect operations, production stability and compliance. Mitigation is improved water recycling and reuse, optimised process water consumption, strengthened rainwater harvesting and development of multiple water sources.
- Digital substitution in writing and printing paper and newsprint — Digital media, e-governance and online education reduce long-term demand for W&P grades, and the shift to digital media consumption may reduce demand for newsprint over time. This bears directly on the segments where the Company holds its stated leadership (premium newsprint) and its Solitaire brand presence. Mitigation is a progressive rebalancing of the product mix toward packaging board and specialty papers to reduce dependence on newsprint.
- Energy cost and asset utilisation — Energy costs constitute a significant portion of operating expenses and are subject to volatility, while sub-optimal utilisation of manufacturing capacity may affect operating efficiency and profitability. Mitigation is captive power generation, proximity to coal sources, ongoing energy-efficiency initiatives and evaluation of alternate energy sources, together with a diversified product portfolio and flexible production planning to optimise utilisation.
- Cybersecurity risk across digital manufacturing and ERP systems — Digital manufacturing systems and ERP platforms (the Company maintains all records in SAP with workflow and approvals routed through it) increase exposure to cyber threats and operational disruption. Mitigation is IT security controls, role-based access, firewalls, endpoint protection, a comprehensive security policy and periodic audits.
- Structural concentration - single plant, single activity — Not labelled as a risk in the AR but disclosed as fact: the BRSR reports 1 plant and no international locations, with 100% of turnover from one activity (manufacturing paper and paperboard, NIC 1701), and the Company has no subsidiary, JV or associate. All manufacturing is at Balasore, Odisha. Exports are only about 5% of turnover across 14 countries, so the business is almost entirely exposed to Indian domestic paper demand and to a single site's operational continuity.
- Talent availability and retention — Availability and retention of skilled manpower are critical for operational continuity and growth in a technically intensive industry. The BRSR classifies talent management as an opportunity rather than a risk, mitigated through structured and on-the-job training, planned job rotation and competency mapping; the MD&A risk table classifies it as Talent Risk. Permanent-employee turnover rose to 9.13% in FY 2025-26 from 5.04% in FY 2024-25 (permanent workers 0.53%).

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells multilayer coated paperboard, newsprint, writing and printing paper and specialty paper, catering to a diversified B2B customer base of packaging converters and processors, food and pharmaceutical product companies, publishers, educational institutions, commercial printers and media houses. It operates as a non-integrated paper mill, sourcing pulp and wastepaper from domestic as well as international markets, with facilities equipped with contemporary paper machines, de-inking capabilities, captive power generation and established environmental management systems. It maintains a strong domestic presence supported by an extensive distribution network and long-standing institutional relationships, while shifting its mix toward value-added and specialty products such as oil and grease resistant papers and pharma inserts.

business.body:
- **Packaging Board:** Multilayer Coated Paperboard, Premium virgin and superior-quality recycled boards, GlamKot Premium (premium version of its Solid Bleached Sulphate (SBS) board offering superior bulk and stiffness), Deep-freeze board (specialty paperboard for ice cream tubs, seafood cartons and frozen meal boxes)
- **Newsprint:** High-quality / premium newsprint
- **Writing & Printing:** Solitaire (premium maplitho), Solitaire Note
- **Specialty Papers (OGR / Pharma):** Oil and Grease Resistant (OGR) paper, including brown OGR grades, OGR Brown Paper (eco-friendly virgin-grade brown packaging material), Pharma insert paper, High-Strength Paper (durable grade for specialised industrial and packaging applications)
- **Kraft Paper:** Low GSM high BF kraft paper and higher GSM grades up to 150 GSM

outlook.body:
- Deepen the specialty product portfolio - OGR grades developed for demanding food-service applications requiring resistance to heat, moisture and grease, and deeper capability in pharma insert paper where print fidelity and dimensional consistency are essential
- Expand into deep-freeze packaging board and cigarette board, described as specialised categories offering sustainable margins and long-term customer relationships
- Increase the contribution of value-added, premium and import-substitute grades to the mix to improve realisations, customer retention and long-term market positioning
- Launch and run Project Unnati, a structured programme covering procurement optimisation, value engineering and manufacturing efficiency across all operational functions, designed to unlock cost efficiencies and improve productivity over the coming years
- Integrate artificial intelligence into manufacturing and management processes covering predictive maintenance, inventory planning, MIS reporting and order fulfilment efficiency
- Shift procurement to FOB-based buying to gain control over freight and shipping decisions, with disciplined engagement with global carriers and tracking of freight indices
- Retain the non-integrated operating model with flexible, geographically diversified global sourcing as a structural hedge against domestic wood cost inflation
- Modernise manufacturing assets and raise the quality benchmark of critical production assets (PM-2 rebuild; transition of pharma-grade production from PM3 to PM2)
- Strengthen the renewable energy footprint and water stewardship as operational priorities alongside CSR in healthcare, education and rural infrastructure
- Continue to evaluate opportunities to strengthen manufacturing capabilities in line with evolving market requirements, while strengthening customer relationships and advancing digital capabilities across the organisation
- The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, published on its website, and states that the FY 2025-26 pay-out is in accordance with that policy: the Board on 28th May 2026 recommended a preference dividend of 8% (Rs 8 per Rs 100 face-value preference share) and an equity dividend of Rs 3.20 per Rs 2 face-value equity share (160%), subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. Unclaimed dividends and the related shares are transferred to the IEPF on the statutory seven-year cycle, with the process and schedule disclosed. The Company did not raise any funds through preferential allotment or qualified institutional placement during FY 2025-26 and has not issued any convertible instruments. It has no subsidiary, so the material-subsidiary policy is not applicable. Executive-director remuneration is framed by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee against external competitive environment, track record, potential and individual and company performance, with incentive remuneration/commission approved by the Board on the NRC's recommendation; no severance fees were paid and no stock options have been issued to any Director. Capital-structure context from the BRSR: paid-up equity share capital of Rs 12.10 crores alongside Non-Convertible Non-Cumulative Redeemable Preference Shares of Rs 35 crores and Optionally Convertible Non-Cumulative Redeemable Preference Shares of Rs 18.75 crores.
- Commissioned a 7 MW Solar Power Plant under the Group Captive Model, expected to reduce the carbon footprint; commercial generation commenced in April 2026 and the plant will supply about 11 million units of green energy annually (provenance: Directors' Report Annexure A, routed to the capex_expansion bundle)
- 16.85% of capital expenditure in FY 2025-26 (14.80% in FY 2024-25) was directed to technologies improving environmental and social impact - effluent treatment infrastructure for wastewater management and compliance, renewable energy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and safety-related upgrades; 100% of R&D expenditure is directed at environmental and social impact of products and processes, focused on process efficiency, resource optimisation, product quality and safer, more sustainable manufacturing (provenance: BRSR Principle 2, routed to the capex_expansion bundle)
- Responsible sourcing - procurement of wood pulp from Forest Stewardship Council (FSC)-certified suppliers, ensuring adherence to globally recognised environmental standards
- Circularity - sustainable sourcing procedures using wastepaper as a key raw material, with investments in wastepaper recycling systems and effluent treatment infrastructure built on circular-economy principles
- Water stewardship - reduction in freshwater consumption through enhanced recycling and reuse of treated process water and ETP effluent; the Year at a Glance strip states 71.05% water treated and reused
- Waste - the Year at a Glance strip states approximately 1,16,000 tonnes of waste material recycled (provenance: Corporate Overview strip, routed to the strategy_outlook and capex_expansion bundles)
- Energy conservation programme delivering measured savings: CPP-grid synchronisation saving about 20 MT/day of process steam; ash-conveying process air cut from 8,500 to 5,500 Nm3/shift (about 1,440 kWh/day); IE-1/IE-2 motors replaced with IE-3 in PM-1; energy-efficient vacuum pump in PM-3 (about 800 kWh/day); additional Board Mill cooling tower (about 1,400 kWh/day); ETP aeration blower motors downsized 160 kW to 132 kW (about 600 kWh/day); ETP sludge used in the boiler as renewable fuel and part of electricity requirement met through green energy procured via power exchanges
- CSR focused on healthcare, education and rural infrastructure development around the plants, with the Year at a Glance strip stating 1,05,200 trees planted, 21,008 students supported and 48 community development programmes conducted; CSR is applicable under Section 135 and the Company has a CSR Policy
- Governance and ethics - Vigil Mechanism and Whistle Blower Policy plus a Code of Conduct published on the website; no complaints received under the whistle-blower mechanism during the reporting period; a Risk Management Committee constituted under Regulation 21 with a Risk Management Policy, which met twice during the year (1st July 2025 and 19th January 2026); in the Board's opinion no risk threatens the existence of the Company
- Grievance redressal - structured mechanisms for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers (Sparsh internal HR portal), customers and value chain partners; 257 customer complaints in FY 2025-26 (332 in FY 2024-25) all resolved, and nil pending at year end across every stakeholder group
- Human rights and safety - value-chain awareness programmes covering 100% of dealers and customers, 90% of suppliers, 100% of contractors and contract workers and 90% of transporters; 98% of employees and 95% of workers covered by health & safety, quality-concept, process and Code of Conduct training
- Social - the Company reports no complaint pertaining to sexual harassment during FY 2025-26 and has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee and adopted a POSH policy; workforce strength 2,875 (1,059 employees and 1,816 workers); women are 20% of the Board (2 of 10) and 2.62% of permanent employees, with no women among permanent workers or KMP
- BRSR assurance - the Company states 'Not Applicable' for reasonable assurance of BRSR Core, assurance provider and type of assurance; reporting boundary is standalone. This is a stated limitation on the ESG data above, not an omission.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 capital work was modernisation-led rather than capacity-additive. The single Balasore, Odisha mill saw a major upgradation of Paper Machine 2: a state-of-the-art auto slice control headbox with MLF for better formation, a new calendaring section with thermo-roll for uniform calliper and smoothness, an added CD profiler for uniform basis weight, moisture and calliper across the deckle, an increase in approach-flow fan pump capacity from 2,200 LPM to 2,600 LPM, and a new tail feeding system from calendar to pope reel. The upgrade raised PM2 machine speed from 510 mpm to 550 mpm and enabled the successful transition of pharma-grade paper production from PM3 to PM2. The headbox was imported from a paper machine manufacturer in Italy and the calendaring section from a manufacturer in Germany; both are stated as successfully commissioned and operating satisfactorily. Board Mill work included an upgraded vacuum separator in the forming section, modified pulper rotor design, upgraded forced lubrication and an additional cooling tower for the water-cooled chillers; PM-1 received a closed-loop nip load controlling system; DIP-3 critical drives were upgraded; an additional decanter was installed in the ETP. On energy, the Company commissioned a 7 MW Solar Power Plant under the Group Captive Model, with commercial generation commencing in April 2026 and the plant expected to supply about 11 million units of green energy annually; the Board's Report describes the same project as commissioned under the open access route. A long list of energy-conservation retrofits was executed (CPP-grid synchronisation saving about 20 MT/day of process steam; ash-conveying process air cut from 8,500 to 5,500 Nm3/shift; IE-3 motor replacements in PM-1; VFD/AC motor conversion at PM-1 Pope Reel; a 45 kW Broke Tower pump replaced with a 30 kW unit in PM-2; an energy-efficient vacuum pump in PM-3; ETP aeration blower motors downsized from 160 kW to 132 kW). The upgrades enabled new product launches - deep-freeze board, GlamKot Premium SBS board, OGR Brown Paper, High-Strength Paper and enhanced pharma insert paper. The Chairman's message adds an expansion into deep-freeze packaging board and cigarette board. Capital investment was stated at Rs 30.29 crores in FY 2025-26 following Rs 20.50 crores in FY 2024-25 across paper machines, control systems and downstream processing infrastructure (provenance: the Whole-time Director and CEO's message, routed to the strategy_outlook bundle, not to this one). The BRSR states that 16.85% of capex in FY 2025-26 (14.80% in FY 2024-25) went into technologies improving environmental and social impact - effluent treatment infrastructure, renewable energy and safety-related upgrades. No new line, machine or greenfield capacity addition with a commissioning timeline is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian paper and paperboard packaging market valued at USD 13.72 billion in FY 2025-26 and projected to reach USD 19.57 billion by FY 2030-31 at a CAGR of approximately 6.13%, which management frames as an opportunity to strengthen its position across value-added and specialty segments
- India's per capita paper consumption at approximately 16 kg, significantly below the global average, described as substantial long-term growth headroom as incomes rise, organised retail expands and formalisation deepens
- Ongoing shift away from single-use plastics, with Extended Producer Responsibility norms and restrictions on plastic packaging imports accelerating substitution of paper and paperboard in food service, e-commerce and consumer goods
- Packaging board demand supported by rising offtake from FMCG, pharmaceutical, food service and e-commerce sectors
- Writing and printing demand supported by institutional demand from education, government and corporate applications, with Solitaire and Solitaire Note retaining market presence
- Specialty segment (OGR and pharma insert) described as high-specification categories where quality requirements are stringent, competition remains limited and customer relationships are built over long periods
- Renewal of nominations from global FMCG companies including Unilever and P&G, cited as evidence of customer confidence in quality and delivery
- Indian paper consumption projected to reach around 30 million tonnes by FY2027, driven mainly by packaging; industry recovery expected from FY26 aided by stabilisation in input costs, despite ongoing import pressures
- Domestic newsprint supply gap - India's annual newsprint demand around 1.2 million tonnes against domestic production struggling to exceed 0.5 million tonnes (about 40% of demand), a gap persisting more than 20 years, creating an import-substitution opening
- Board's Report headwinds: continued import pressure from low-cost origins, subdued realisations across certain product segments and persistent volatility in raw material and energy costs; turnover was marginally lower on net sales realisation pressure across the domestic paper industry
- Long-term outlook for the Indian paper industry described as positive, supported by rising literacy, increasing organised retail penetration, demand for sustainable packaging and policy support under the National Education Policy (NEP 2020)
- Global macro backdrop flagged as a swing factor: trade-policy uncertainty resurfacing in February 2026 after the US Supreme Court ruling on import tariffs, and geopolitical tension in West Asia disrupting energy routes including the Strait of Hormuz, pressuring oil, gas and fertiliser markets

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table flags cheap imports from China and ASEAN as putting pressure on domestic prices and margins, with negative financial implication. The Board's Report independently describes the year as marked by continued import pressure from low-cost origins and subdued realisations across certain product segments, and turnover was marginally lower on net sales realisation pressure. Mitigation is quality differentiation, focus on specification-driven customers and pursuit of trade-remedy support through industry associations.

This is the structural exposure of a non-integrated mill. Pulp, wastepaper, chemicals and packaging inputs are exposed to global commodity and domestic price volatility, and the MD&A risk table adds that fluctuations in global pulp and wastepaper prices may impact input costs and margins. Mitigation is a diversified sourcing strategy across geographies and suppliers, long-term arrangements, term contracts with selective spot purchases, inventory planning and selective hedging.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility (pulp, wastepaper, chemicals)

risks.note: USD-linked imports create a mismatch against INR revenues; rupee depreciation increases landed input cost. This is amplified by the quality-led model built on imported virgin wood pulp and imported machinery, against exports of only about 5% of turnover, so there is little natural offset. Mitigation is hedging through forward contracts and other approved instruments under the treasury policy, plus natural hedging mechanisms.

Compliance with effluent, EPR, ZLD and environmental norms requires continuous investment, and the Company is subject to evolving environmental laws which may impact operations. Mitigation is a dedicated compliance team, internal audit review and management systems aligned with relevant certifications, supported by continuous monitoring and process upgrades.

Water is a critical input for paper manufacturing, and scarcity, cost escalation or regulatory restrictions can affect operations, production stability and compliance. Mitigation is improved water recycling and reuse, optimised process water consumption, strengthened rainwater harvesting and development of multiple water sources.

Digital media, e-governance and online education reduce long-term demand for W&P grades, and the shift to digital media consumption may reduce demand for newsprint over time. This bears directly on the segments where the Company holds its stated leadership (premium newsprint) and its Solitaire brand presence. Mitigation is a progressive rebalancing of the product mix toward packaging board and specialty papers to reduce dependence on newsprint.
risks.risk: Digital substitution in writing and printing paper and newsprint

risks.note: Energy costs constitute a significant portion of operating expenses and are subject to volatility, while sub-optimal utilisation of manufacturing capacity may affect operating efficiency and profitability. Mitigation is captive power generation, proximity to coal sources, ongoing energy-efficiency initiatives and evaluation of alternate energy sources, together with a diversified product portfolio and flexible production planning to optimise utilisation.

Digital manufacturing systems and ERP platforms (the Company maintains all records in SAP with workflow and approvals routed through it) increase exposure to cyber threats and operational disruption. Mitigation is IT security controls, role-based access, firewalls, endpoint protection, a comprehensive security policy and periodic audits.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity risk across digital manufacturing and ERP systems
